recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core follow-up is needed unless FHIR-I decides to reopen the broader design question of whether Binary.securityContext should be renamed, replaced by security labels, or moved to an extension.
issue_request: FHIR-14563 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-I change request for Binary, raised against STU3, asking for the Binary.securityContext explanation to clarify what the element means, when it is appropriate or redundant, and how it relates to resources such as DocumentReference/Media and security labels. The approved resolution was to replace the element definition/comment with text describing another resource as a proxy for Binary access-control sensitivity and explaining circumstances where automatic rules from referencing resources are or are not sufficient.
initial_application: The issue was applied by 22764b92f28e8e450712ccdd2561b6f8827223da, GF#14563 - fix definition of Binary.securityContext, which changed source/binary/binary-spreadsheet.xml with the approved short definition, proxy-resource definition, and comment. Jira's implementation comment records svn 14337, matching that git-svn commit. The source was later converted from the spreadsheet to source/binary/structuredefinition-Binary.xml and the substantive FHIR-14563 text was carried forward.
additional_context: Binary is active in source/fhir.ini, so the inspected StructureDefinition and narrative files are current build inputs. The current definition and comment explain the proxy-resource access-control semantics, and the Binary narrative says securityContext/X-Security-Context tells the server to treat the Binary as another resource. The approved 2018 wording mentioned Media, but GF#19250 later merged Media into DocumentReference and removed Media from this example. Neighboring Binary security issues FHIR-16890 and FHIR-17833 are already represented on the combined branch and do not require changing this element definition.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source already conveys that Binary.securityContext is a Reference to another resource used as an access-control proxy, can point to related or unrelated resources, and is not required when server-side knowledge from existing references is sufficient. Re-adding the obsolete Media example or duplicating the guidance in narrative prose would not change implementer understanding.
